incidents.root_cause: TB-BH wireless backhaul link to the core site degraded (signal -82 to -89 dBm warnings) and then dropped; TB-AP1 and TB-BH were silent until the link returned
RF interference on TA-AP1 wlan1 at 5785 MHz (source not identified in the logs); cleared by an admin channel change to 5825 MHz
Repeated SSH login attempts against CORE-RTR from 192.0.2.88; all 12 attempts failed

test_questions.q: What warnings appeared on TB-BH before the Tower B outage, and when?
test_questions.a: Three bh-signal-check script warnings: 01:56:29 (-82 dBm), 02:02:53 (-85 dBm), 02:07:41 (-89 dBm).

test_questions.q: When did TB-BH and TB-AP1 stop sending logs, and when did they resume?
test_questions.a: The last line from Tower B devices was TB-BH at 02:10:17 (disconnected, extensive data loss). Nothing came from TB-BH or TB-AP1 until TB-BH connected at 04:35:31.

test_questions.q: When did the first Tower B PPPoE session drop in the overnight outage, and when did the last one reconnect?
test_questions.a: The first drop (terminating, peer not responding) was at 02:10:22. The last session reconnected at 04:40:08. All 15 Tower B customers were affected.

test_questions.q: Which source IP attacked CORE-RTR over SSH, how many login failures were logged, and when?
test_questions.a: 192.0.2.88. There were 12 failures from 19:20:36 to 19:29:22 (users: admin x8, root x2, support x1, user x1), each preceded by a firewall SYN line to port 22.

test_questions.q: Which Tower A customers lost their PPPoE session during the afternoon interference, and what ended it?
test_questions.a: cust-A003, A006, A009, A012 and A015 (11 PPPoE disconnects between 14:21:00 and 15:02:53). An admin logged in to TA-AP1 at 15:01:26 and changed the wlan1 frequency from 5785 to 5825 at 15:03:02.

test_questions.q: When did CORE-RTR log high-CPU warnings?
What external device or source caused the interference on TA-AP1?
